chunk_findings.detail: The new return claims coverage while the code has already proven that the tests this change reaches were *not* run by ci. `rest = _not_run(sel.tests, _regression(st, it), done)` is reached only after the early `if not rest: return covered`, and the truncation check immediately above guarantees `ran["tests"]` is a complete list, so a non-empty `rest` means those reached tests are genuinely absent from ci's recorded run. If `run_command` cannot turn the item's command into a pytest invocation (e.g. `unit_tests = "make unit"`, `tox`, `scripts/test.py`), the new code returns `Scope("covered", "…ci's selected run stands")` and the gate passes without ever running `rest`. Concrete input: `ran = {"scope":"selected","selected":1,"tests":["tests/x.py"],"always_tests":[]}`, `sel.tests == ["tests/x.py","tests/y.py"]`, command `"make unit"` → `rest == [y.py]`, `run_command` is falsy, and `y.py` is silently skipped; before this change the branch returned `"full"` and the whole-suite fallback did execute `y.py`. The message "ci's selected run stands" is a promise the code does not keep: by construction this branch is only reachable when ci did not take those tests, so a regression reached only through `y.py` now passes the gate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testscope.py:263-267 (`if not cmd:` branch)

chunk_findings.detail: When `int(ran.get("selected")) > len(done)` the record's test list is cut, so nothing in the data says that the tests the change reaches (`sel.tests`) were among the `selected` tests that actually ran. The old code was wrong to return `"full"` here (that is the whole-suite timeout this bug is about), but the stated fix is to "run the selected scope (tests the change reaches) or take the ci result as evidence"; the selected scope is computable in this branch (`rest = _not_run(sel.tests, _regression(st, it), done)`), and the code instead runs neither: it returns `"covered"` and never executes `rest`. Concrete input: `ran = {"selected":5,"tests":["tests/other.py"]}`, item reaches `tests/a.py` → scope `"covered"`, `a.py` never runs, even though the only known thing is that the list was truncated, not that `a.py` was covered. The recorded evidence is unverifiable for the reached set, so the "covered" verdict is asserted without support.

chunk_findings.detail: The tool path was patched for the same bug id (Be81c39acb8), but for exactly the case the helper's own docstring promises to preserve it still runs the primary checkout. Take an agent that holds one live lease on T1 and calls the `ddflow_ci` tool with `action="run"` and no ref *from T1's worktree*, so `called_from` is T1's tree path. `held_item(repo, agent, called_from)` computes `held == ["T1"]` but then returns `""`, because the design (and the docstring "A caller standing in a tree that is an item's own keeps that tree's HEAD") deliberately bails out when `_item_here(st, "HEAD", where, repo)` says the caller is in an item's tree. So `ref` stays the literal `"HEAD"` and `run(repo, ref="HEAD", called_from=<T1 tree>, …)` is called. `run` does not resolve refs against `called_from` — that is precisely why the CLI surface next door has to compute `SS.head_here_or_repo(c.repo, where)` and pass the tree's own ref instead of `"HEAD"` (the pre-existing `ref = a.ref or SS.head_here_or_repo(c.repo, where)` line that the CLI bug existed behind). Consequently the tool resolves `HEAD` against `repo`, reports the primary's sha and runs the primary's tree — the same wrong-ref/wrong-tree outcome the comment on this added line claims to fix. The CLI path never has this hole because `held_item` returning `""` falls through to `SS.head_here_or_repo(c.repo, where)`; the tool has no such fallback, so `held_item` returning `""` for in-tree callers is silently ignored there and `"HEAD"` wins. Note the added test only exercises the CLI surface, so it cannot catch this.

chunk_findings.detail: The new early return claims `Scope("covered", …, covered_by="ci selected run {sha}")` whenever this gate's own selection cannot be enumerated (`sel is None`) or has collapsed to the whole suite (`sel.full`), without ever consulting the ci record's test list or the item's regression test. The only thing actually proven before this point is that the ci gate ran *some* selected selection on this commit and passed; nothing in the data says that selection covers the tests this change reaches. Concretely: take the hub-change / post-merge case the intent names — ci runs and passes a selected run on commit C recording, say, `tests=[t1,t2]` (its base was an older ref); the item's base ref then advances (a main merge), so `select(tree, base, …)` now returns `sel.full` ("the change reaches 137 files, over the limit") on the *same* commit C. The code returns `covered` with `covered_by="ci selected run C"`, so `ddflow gate run <item> unit_tests` passes while t3…t137 — and, worse, the item's own recorded regression test, which the earlier logic checks via `_not_run(sel.tests, _regression(st, it), done)` — are never run: this branch returns before that check, so a regression test that the ci selected run did not take is silently skipped and the gate still reports coverage. The old code returned `Scope("full", f"{why}: only the whole suite keeps recall")` here precisely because with no enumeration you cannot know the ci selection was a superset. Note this contradicts the change's own module docstring, which still lists "a selection that cannot be made: no base, git cannot say what changed, no test reaches the change" among the cases that run the whole suite, and it is inconsistent with the author's own resolution of the `if not cmd:` branch (where non-run tests correctly produce `Scope("full", …)`, not a coverage claim): here, with strictly less information available, coverage is claimed. Fix: in this branch, either fall back to the item's own command, or return covered only after

chunk_findings.detail: The new early return claims `Scope("covered", …, covered_by="ci selected run {sha}")` whenever this gate's own selection cannot be enumerated (`sel is None`) or has collapsed to the whole suite (`sel.full`), without ever consulting the ci record's test list or the item's regression test. The only thing actually proven before this point is that the ci gate ran *some* selected selection on this commit and passed; nothing in the data says that selection covers the tests this change reaches. Concretely: take the hub-change / post-merge case the intent names — ci runs and passes a selected run on commit C recording, say, `tests=[t1,t2]` (its base was an older ref); the item's base ref then advances (a main merge), so `select(tree, base, …)` now returns `sel.full` ("the change reaches 137 files, over the limit") on the *same* commit C. The code returns `covered` with `covered_by="ci selected run C"`, so `ddflow gate run <item> unit_tests` passes while t3…t137 — and, worse, the item's own recorded regression test, which the earlier logic checks via `_not_run(sel.tests, _regression(st, it), done)` — are never run: this branch returns before that check, so a regression test that the ci selected run did not take is silently skipped and the gate still reports coverage. The old code returned `Scope("full", f"{why}: only the whole suite keeps recall")` here precisely because with no enumeration you cannot know the ci selection was a superset. Note this contradicts the change's own module docstring, which still lists "a selection that cannot be made: no base, git cannot say what changed, no test reaches the change" among the cases that run the whole suite, and it is inconsistent with the author's own resolution of the `if not cmd:` branch (where non-run tests correctly produce `Scope("full", …)`, not a coverage claim): here, with strictly less information available, coverage is claimed. Fix: in this branch, either fall back to the item's own command, or return covered only after

chunk_findings.detail: The new guard treats an explicit `ref="HEAD"` as if no ref had been given. Given an agent holding exactly one live lease and a call `ddflow_ci(action="run", ref="HEAD")` from outside any item worktree (for example from the primary checkout, so `_item_here` does not return an item), `held_item` returns that one held item id, and `held_item(...) or ref` replaces the requested `"HEAD"` with the item id. The run then targets the held item's branch rather than repository HEAD. The CLI path preserves the distinction: `a.ref or AR.held_item(...)` treats `"HEAD"` as an explicit ref and skips `held_item`, so the same request via the CLI does run `HEAD`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/cirun.py:158

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test only commits `w.txt` at the repository root, but `_item_with_ci` creates task `T1` with `--globs src/**` and `src/x.py`; `w.txt` does not affect any T1 gate work. A partial fix that reports the worktree/HEAD SHA correctly for the report but still executes the pipeline against the primary checkout would still pass this test: `src/x.py` is unchanged between the two trees, so `body["recorded"]["ok"]` and `gate["outcome"]` remain `passed`. The test therefore does not protect the “and ran main's tree” half of bug Be81c39acb8.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_gate.py:355

chunk_findings.detail: The fix treats an explicitly supplied `ref="HEAD"` as “no ref given” and overrides it with the held item id. Concrete failure: an agent holds one live lease on `T1`, and calls `ddflow_ci(action="run", ref="HEAD", called_from=<primary checkout>)`. `held_item` returns `"T1"`, so the run executes T1’s branch. The same change’s CLI path (`ddflow/surfaces/commands/ci.py`) intentionally preserves explicit `"HEAD"` because `a.ref or ...` is truthy, passing `HEAD` to `AR.run`. Thus the same caller-visible ref value runs different branches through the two entry points, and the comment “no ref given” is not true for `"HEAD"`.
